images.title: Rice bags in eighths
images.purpose: Show the method cue for ordering from largest to smallest: weigh every bag in the same unit, here eighths of a kilogram.
images.composition: One upright scale at the left, and three upright rice bags standing on one baseline to its right, heaviest first, with wide gaps.
images.exact_structure: Left: one upright scale from 0 to 1 kg with 9 evenly spaced tick marks, 0 to 8/8, drawn in grey #6B7280. Right: three plain rectangular rice bags of equal width standing on the same baseline as the scale's 0, each bag's height matching the scale: the first 6 ticks tall filled teal #0072B2, the second 5 ticks tall filled amber #E69F00, the third 4 ticks tall filled reddish purple #CC79A7. Exactly 1 scale, 9 ticks, 3 bags.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any of the question sets, their rewritten forms or their order shown anywhere
images.takeaway: In one common unit, the heaviest bag has the biggest numerator.
images.description: Three rice bags of 3/4 kg, 5/8 kg and 1/2 kg stand against a scale marked in eighths, at 6, 5 and 4 eighths, heaviest first.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to read each bag on the scale in eighths and say why the order goes down from left to right.

image_decisions.why: The rice bag demo on one scale gives the descending order method without working either question set.
